A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DSSP-RAG, with matching methodology, equations, original experiments and appendix material. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of all substantive material, including the later additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA and public-health benchmark results, component ablations, efficiency measurements and analyses of internal representations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds ASQA evaluation, knowledge-conflict experiments, component comparisons, threshold sensitivity results and case studies.

M1.justification: The JSD-based detector, Energy Quotient filtering, shared/private mixed attention, fusion procedure and training loss remain unchanged. DSSP-only configurations and component replacements are introduced as experimental controls; adaptive threshold selection is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: v2 retains the five original datasets and adds ASQA, extending evaluation to long-form answers requiring factual grounding and discourse-level generation. Section 4.3.2 also introduces a distinct synthetic test scenario with deliberately incorrect statements in retrieved contexts.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 introduces evaluated comparisons against EditCoT and CK-PLUG. Table 5 adds Hyb-Cons as a hallucination-detection replacement and entropy-based and attention-based filtering replacements. These substantially expand component-specific comparisons while retaining the original main benchmark comparators.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include disabling detection and filtering for DSSP-only comparisons, inserting two incorrect context statements and measuring ConR/ParR/EM, and evaluating ASQA with str-em and R-L. Appendix C adds a threshold sweep from 0.6 to 1.5 in 0.1 increments. The original reported training settings, splits, backbones and retrieval setup remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled knowledge-conflict stress tests, alternative detector/filter comparisons and detection-threshold sensitivity analysis. Appendix G adds paired outputs with and without DSSP, extending illustrative queries already present in v1. These provide substantial new diagnostic evidence beyond the retained component-removal, document-count and layer analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same paired t-test criterion, p < 0.05, and significance markings in Table 1. v2 introduces no additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for conflict tests, component replacements, ASQA, threshold sensitivity and paired cases. For example, Table 9 reports LLaMA3 DSSP_AR ASQA str-em/R-L of 42.9/43.3 versus SEAKR's 40.1/40.6. In the retained ablation table, DSSP's 2Wiki F1 changes from 37.6 to 37.8, while TriviaQA EM changes from 54.5 to 55.4 for DSSP and from 55.4 to 54.5 for Trained Probes. Main Tables 1–2 and efficiency results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The method and loss equations, JSD/KL definitions and properties, and mixed-attention operator derivation are retained. v1 Appendices B and D correspond to v2 Appendices C and E; their mathematical substance is unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same central contribution claims: integrating unsupervised hallucination detection, knowledge filtering and shared/private mixed attention to mitigate knowledge conflicts and improve RAG performance. Abstract and conclusion revisions preserve these claims; the additional experiments supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation for the retained HotpotQA deficit against SEAKR, interpretations of the new conflict and long-form results, and explanations of threshold-dependent retrieval failures. Appendix C discusses adaptive threshold calibration as future work. Existing limitations concerning consistently wrong answers and excessive retrieved noise remain.

D1.justification: The Table 1 caption newly specifies that Self-RAG was fine-tuned from LLaMA2-7B-chat using NQ-style data, documenting an existing comparison. Hardware, training sample counts, optimization hyperparameters, retrieval corpus and prompt templates are retained, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting CK-PLUG, Hyb-Cons, filtering comparators and ASQA, alongside contextual citations, and removes Qiao et al. (2023). New discussion contrasts DSSP with chain-of-thought editing, entropy-based reliance and alternative filters, while preserving the paper's overall positioning within RAG and hallucination mitigation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion receive localized rewrites, terminology and model names are standardized, and affiliations, contact information and acknowledgments change. A conflict-evaluation subsection and ASQA/case-study appendices are inserted, but the existing narrative and most methodological and appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables presenting conflict-method comparisons, knowledge-reliance controls, ASQA results, threshold sensitivity and paired cases. The ablation table expands into separate detection and filtering groups, and retained displays are repositioned. Existing diagrams, heatmaps, plots and prompt figures are preserved; the substantial display expansion is concentrated in experimental tables.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's general benchmark and ablation evidence, v2 provides more direct tests of the central conflict-resolution claim through DSSP-only comparisons and deliberately corrupted contexts. Component replacements and ASQA also strengthen validation. The gain is limited by underdescribed new evaluation protocols and an unresolved mathematical inconsistency: Appendix C states that JSD lies in [0,1], while the new Table 11 tests thresholds above 1 without explaining a rescaling.
